script.name: Lib.Cmd.StockExchange.Updater
script.description: Lib Cmd: Fluctuates the stock exchange's stock values

line.comment: * SCRIPT NAME: Lib.Cmd.StockExchange.Updater
* DESCRIPTION: Task 348. Updates the stock exchange using the owning race's factories.
* Factory health sets a target position within the stock's price band.
* Prices retain their normal random movement but are biased toward that target.
* AUTHOR: Litcube (Modified by Mordan in FoF, ported to Expanded 2.2)
* DATE: 11 February 2013
* write to player logbook: printf: fmt='%s is running Stock Exchange Updater, version: %s', [THIS], $Version, null, null, null

line.text: '%s is stopping Stock Exchange Updater, version: %s: No Stock Exchange info for this stock exchange found!'

line.comment: * Everything below is initialized here rather than only inside the subroutines.
* A variable assigned solely in a subroutine trips the compiler's linear unassigned-variable check.
* Stock market tuning.
* Working variables.
* the Gbl.StockExchange will run us again

line.text: '%s is stopping Stock Exchange Updater, version: %s: No Stock Exchange info for this stock exchange found!'

line.comment: * Rescan the economy periodically.
* Faction industry does not change fast enough to justify a factory scan every tick.
* Measures the owning race's industrial health, sets $targetIndex, and publishes the economy indicators used by the Stock Exchange menu.
* Expanded 2.2: Unlike in FoF, only factories belonging to the Stock Exchange's owner count.
* This has two effects:
* 1. The market reflects the owning faction's economy, encouraging the player to invest in and support its industry.
* 2. Player-owned and foreign factories cannot directly affect that faction's share prices.
* No factories remain. Bottom of the target range, not the price floor itself.
* Check every factory owned by the faction. This scan runs infrequently, and using the
* full industrial base keeps the economic target deterministic while stock movement remains random.
* Compress factory health into the configured target range rather than the full 0..100 band.
* Mapping onto the full band would pin a dead economy against the floor clamp and a thriving
* one against the ceiling, leaving the random walk nowhere to move at either extreme.
* Expanded scales the target range directly to avoid intermediate integer truncation.
* A factory counts as unhealthy if ANY of its wares sits at 0% or 100%.
* There is no engine query for production state, so ware storage extremes are used
* as a proxy for production being starved or stalled.
* Requires $Stock. One step of the biased walk, then Litcube's Change: does the rest.
* Full lean applies once the stock index is $pullFullDistance points from its fundamental target.
* With $pullMax = 20, the maximum directional bias is 70/30.

line.text: ' | Index: %s | Target: %s | Distance: %s | Lean: %s | Up chance: %s'

line.comment: * Only half of the ticks move at all, so the price is not in constant motion.
* Same step size Litcube used, so each stock's market cap still sets how coarsely it moves.
* The +1 is used to compensate for random value from X to Y decrementing Y by 1 if Y is a variable.
* Menu.StockExchange.SM colours the traded price off the sign of Stock[12] - green when
* rising, red when falling. Feeding it the distance to target keeps that indicator live
* and now makes it mean something: which way the faction's economy is pulling this stock.
* Requires Stock, Change
